title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and manager guidance for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and core people policies. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineering leaders responsible for execution and compliance.

Owners and SLAs
- Document owner: People Operations (people-ops@redwood.com)
- Hiring SLA: initial interview scheduling within 72 hours of candidate screen; offer turnaround target 3 business days after final approval; time-to-offer target < 30 days for IC roles, < 45 days for senior/lead roles.
- Onboarding SLA: new hire account provisioning (Airtable/Slack/GitHub) within 2 business days of start date; equipment shipped 5 business days prior to start for remote hires when requested.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
Intro: Our hiring process balances speed, candidate experience, and structured evaluation to reduce bias and ensure role fit. Use this as the canonical checklist for all hires.

1.1 Job Requisition and Approval - Hiring manager creates a job requisition in Workday (or our ATS) with role profile, level rubric, and target compensation band. People-ops approvals required: Hiring headcount confirmation, compensation sign-off from Finance, and final posting approval from the hiring manager's director. Templates: use the job description template (linked in related pages).

1.2 Sourcing and Screening - Sourcing channels: internal referrals (highest priority), careers site, LinkedIn Recruiter, university pipelines, partner agencies (as approved). First screen: 30-minute phone/video screen by recruiter to assess fundamentals, compensation expectations, and basic role fit. Recruiter completes the Candidate Intake form and assigns the candidate to the hiring manager for a technical screen when appropriate. Schedule targets: recruiter to schedule first interview within 72 hours of candidate qualification.

1.3 Interview Loop and Scorecards - Interview loop should be no more than 3 onsite/virtual interviews for standard IC roles (recruiter screen + hiring manager/technical + final behavioral/culture interview). For specialized or senior roles, include architecture deep-dive and cross-functional partner interview. Use structured scorecards for every interview. Scorecards must include: technical skills (or role-relevant competencies), behavioral indicators, role-specific rubric (leveling), and 'strengths/risks' free-text fields. Interview calibration: hiring managers must calibrate scoring with their People Partner when hiring for level 5+ or manager roles.

1.4 Decisioning and Offer - Decision meeting: hiring manager convenes interviewers within 48 hours of final interview to review scorecards and make a hire/no-hire decision. Offer approval: hiring manager submits recommended offer to People-ops with candidate name, proposed comp, and any sign-on/relocation requests. People-ops coordinates approvals with Finance and Legal. Offer execution: People-ops sends the offer letter and target acceptance follow-up within 3 business days after approval. For senior hires, Compensation committee sign-off may add 1-3 business days.

1.5 Rejection / Candidate Experience - Provide timely feedback: recruiters should send a courteous rejection within 5 business days of final decision. Maintain candidate pipeline: for near-miss candidates, add tags in ATS for future nurture.

Checklist (high-level, numbered):
1. Requisition + approvals in ATS
2. Job posted + sourcing plan
3. Recruiter screen completed (Candidate Intake)
4. Structured interview loop scheduled
5. Scorecards completed and collected
6. Decision meeting within 48 hours
7. Offer approvals + offer sent within 3 business days

2) Employee onboarding (first 90 days)
Purpose: Ensure new hires are productive and feel supported, with clear role expectations and connections to team and company.

2.1 Pre-boarding (0-7 days before start) - People-ops tasks: create employee record, initiate I-9/remote verification tasks, order equipment/credentials, create accounts (Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub, Atlassian) and shared mailbox access. Hiring manager tasks: share first-week schedule, team intro note, role objectives, and pre-reads (architecture docs, team roadmap).

2.2 Day 1-7: Orientation and Essentials - Company orientation (People-ops): benefits overview, payroll, policies, security training, and required compliance modules (complete by Day 7). Team onboarding (Hiring manager): role kickoff, access to team runbooks, codebase tours, and assignment of a peer buddy. Checklist (Day 1): workstation access confirmed, Slack profile setup, calendar invites for recurring 1:1s scheduled.

2.3 Week 2-4: Role Ramp and Early Goals - First deliverable: small scoped task or bug to complete within 2-4 weeks to validate environment and workflow. 30-day check-in: hiring manager meets with new hire (30-minute checkpoint) to review ramp progress, blockers, and feedback. People-ops runs a quick onboarding survey to capture experience metrics.

2.4 Month 1-3: Performance and Integration - 60-day check-in: deeper review of objectives, training plan adjustments, and career development conversation. 90-day review: formal manager assessment using the new-hire 90-day rubric (competency, cultural fit, initial impact). Decision points include: confirm regular status, extend probation (if applicable), or initiate PIP (rare).

2.5 Onboarding Templates (textual table)
- "Pre-boarding checklist": account provisioning, equipment delivery, NDA signed, core policies reviewed.
- "First-week schedule" example: Day 1: orientation + team lunch; Day 2: systems access + small task; Day 3: architecture deep-dive; Day 4: meet cross-functional partners; Day 5: first-week retro with manager.

3) Performance and feedback cycles
High-level cadence: continuous feedback + quarterly manager reviews + annual calibration. Our goal is frequent, timely feedback with clear calibration across levels.

3.1 Continuous feedback and 1:1s - Managers should hold a weekly or bi-weekly 1:1 with direct reports. Standard 1:1 agenda: wins, blockers, priorities, career coaching, pulse. Encourage real-time praise and redirection via Slack or short written notes. Use peer recognition for observable impact.

3.2 Formal review cadence - Quarterly reviews: each IC receives a short-form performance checkpoint focused on objectives and competency progress; useful for promotion considerations and bonus eligibility. Annual review: comprehensive assessment covering impact, role complexity, strengths, development areas, and compensation recommendations. Calibration: People-ops runs bi-annual calibration cycles for all managers to align role-level expectations and promotion criteria.

3.3 Performance Improvement and PIP - When persistent performance issues are identified, managers should: 1) document concerns and prior coaching, 2) partner with People-ops and Legal, 3) create a Performance Improvement Plan with measurable objectives and review intervals (30/60/90 days). PIP ownership: manager sets weekly checkpoints; People-ops monitors compliance and provides resources (training, mentoring).

3.4 Promotion and leveling - Promotion criteria map to the company career framework: impact, ownership, technical scope, and organizational influence. Managers should prepare a promotion packet (examples, evidence, peer feedback) for People-ops and calibration review.

4) Manager playbook and expected behaviors
This section consolidates core responsibilities and recommended practices for Redwood managers.

4.1 Hiring manager responsibilities - Define role and success metrics before opening a requisition. Own the interview loop quality: prepare structured interview questions and ensure scorecards are used. Provide fast, clear decisions and timely feedback to candidates.

4.2 Day-to-day management - Weekly 1:1s, regular feedback, and clear goal-setting. Career development: own career conversations and create individual development plans at least once per quarter. Recognition and retention: proactive check-ins with high performers and mitigation plans for at-risk employees.

4.3 Coaching and difficult conversations - Use the model: Observe -> Document -> Discuss -> Agree -> Follow-up. Keep records of performance conversations in the manager's private notes and inform People-ops for escalation. Escalation path: manager -> People Partner -> Director of People -> Legal (if needed).

4.4 Interviewer training and bias mitigation - All interviewers must complete our unconscious bias and structured interviewing training modules annually. Use standardized questions, scoring rubrics, and diverse interview panels whenever possible.

5) People policies (quick reference)
- Work hours and flexibility: core hours 10:00-16:00 local time; flexible start/end times agreed with manager.
- Paid time off: standard policy summarized in the HR benefits page (linked).
- Parental leave: extended parental leave policy as defined in benefits summary.
- Remote/Hybrid expectations: defined in the Remote Work policy; managers approve regular remote schedules consistent with team needs.

6) Metrics and reporting
People-ops tracks these KPIs monthly and shares with leadership: time-to-hire, offer acceptance rate, new-hire retention at 90 days, onboarding satisfaction score, manager 1:1 compliance, and internal mobility rate. Targets are set annually during budgeting.

7) Templates and examples (appendix)
- Interview scorecard (example fields): Candidate name, role, interviewer, rubric scores (1-5), evidence, strengths & risks, hire/no-hire recommendation.
- 30/60/90 onboarding template: objectives, success criteria, stakeholders, checkpoints, and learning resources.

Process links and references
- People-ops documentation hub: people-ops@redwood.com (contact)
- Recruiting ATS guide: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/recruiting-ats-guide

Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Who approves offers above band?
A: Compensation committee and Finance sign-off required for offers outside published bands.

Q: What if equipment is delayed?
A: Manager provides a temporary access plan and People-ops escalates fulfillment; remote new hires may receive a stipend where shipping delays persist.
